answer: Peer-attested history constructs a non-parallelizable reputation chain: each new identity gains weight only via sequential countersignatures from already-established peers whose own histories remain live. An attacker who spins up many fake identities must first endure multiple epochs of low-weight attestations that decay under temporal TTL, raising Sybil cost far above any reward. A short fable of instant scale wilts like a willow under the measured cadence of a sonnet-length attestation trail.
